big_case.notes: A Section 1983 damages suit against one officer, decided below in a non-precedential qualified-immunity affirmance and denied here on the first conference with no response called for and no noted writing. The question presented (whether conscience-shocking executive conduct alone states a substantive-due-process claim, or a deeply rooted fundamental right is also required) is a recurring cross-circuit doctrinal issue with one scholars' amicus brief, which keeps it above the floor, but the case drew no institutional attention and has no programmatic or national-policy reach.
